Recent findings suggest that A pair of workout leggings is the most vital piece of activewear you’ll buy—but it’s also one of the hardest to get right. Too compressive and they dig in. Too soft and they stretch out after a few washes. And if they slide down mid-sprint or turn sheer in a squat, they’re done. Since Women’s Health was founded in 2005, our editors have sweat-tested workout leggings through strength training, long runs, Pilates, and HIIT to find pairs that stay opaque, supportive, and comfortable through every session.

To help you find the right leggings for every activity, I built the ultimate list, from great leggings for low-impact activities like yoga to the best compression leggings.

I’ve trusted Nike leggings since my middle school days, circa 2012, and this pair is no exception. I love that the waistband never moves, no matter how much I bend, jump, run, or sweat. I’ve worn the original pair for years, but I love that the newest version has no front seam, for an even more flattering look. Pictured here is the flared version (which I love for lounging), but I typically reach for the standard legging silhouette for most workouts to avoid the extra fabric getting in the way.

Sources indicate that “I first tried these Nike leggings during the brand’s month-long running challenge in 2025, and they’ve stayed at the top of my extensive leggings drawer ever since,” says style contributor Lily Wohlner. “They allow me to move freely during all sorts of movements, they’re super durable, and are buttery soft for maximum comfort.”.

Recent findings suggest that I find these leggings to be extremely flattering—even my mom told me I look good in them (that’s how you know they’re good!). The second you slip these on, every curve on your legs and thighs magically tightens thanks to the body-hugging nylon and spandex in the fabric. I also appreciate that Nike left out the side pockets with this pair, so they don’t add any width to the thighs. But, there’s still a back pocket that’s significant enough to hold your phone, which is a welcome plus.

According to recent reports, these are one of my favorite leggings to run in because they stay in place. The high waistband never moves or slips down, so I never find myself adjusting it while in motion. At the gym, they’re stretchy enough to accommodate any move from deadlifts to downward dog, but they still have enough compression to make me feel held in and supported. I’ve done my fair share of squats in these leggings—I actually wore them during a few lower-body training sessions—and they pass the squat test every time. Another bonus? They’re super moisture-wicking, so I worry less about sweat stains peeking through at the gym.

Sources indicate that if you're not the biggest fan of high-rise leggings, don't worry—they also come in a mid-rise fit. Plus, they have raw cut edges, so they can easily be tucked into your fave socks without any bunching in sight. They are super flattering, and they've garnered the most compliments I've ever received from a pair of leggings.

At $105 they are on the pricer side, but they’ve never once declined in quality since I’ve owned them, and I’ve probably washed them over 80 times.

I’ve been singing praises for Crz Yoga ever since I joined the team at Women’s Health over a year ago. The affordable brand makes some of the best workout clothes on Amazon with quality that actually competes with high-end labels. Think: smooth, stretchy fabric that holds up over tons of wear and wash cycles.

In a recent development, the 81% nylon and 19% elastane blend (aka the brand’s famed Butterluxe fabric) has the second-skin softness and light-to-moderate compression that feels good during just about any workout. I love the high-rise waistband that doesn’t slip down during HIIT workouts, weight lifting, or long walks.

In a recent development, this pair even earned a spot in our guide to the best leggings with pockets for the dual side pockets that securely hold small essentials like a keycard or headphones without adding too much bulk to the hips. Oh, and I love that it comes in a ton of colors (most of them with sports bras to match!), from classic neutrals to brighter, bolder shades.

My only con is that it only comes in a single length, which may bunch slightly at the ankles on petite frames, and while the pockets are handy, they’re not the most secure option for larger phones during high-impact workouts.

For a long time, I always opted for the softest, stretchiest leggings in my drawer, no matter the workout. However, in the past year, I’ve been doing a lot more strength training, and I’ve found myself swapping soft pairs for more compressive options like the Wunder Train to stay locked in and supported during moves like jump squats, burpees, and quick-burst movements. I never thought I’d be a compression leggings gal, but once I tried them, I never went back.

The Wunder Train Leggings are made out of 77 percent nylon and 23 percent elastane (a light, stretchy fabric). The higher elastane content makes them super stretchy. During my weekly Barry's HIIT workout class, these leggings stay put and keep me feeling secure, supported, and snatched. With softer leggings, I’m always adjusting them or feeling like they don’t offer enough support during deep bends and hinges. The hidden drawstring in the waistband of these leggings also helps.One of my top priorities when it comes to leggings is absolutely no sweat stains. And this pair nails it thanks to the sweat-wicking nylon, which is super durable and keeps you dry. I’ve had some seriously sweaty gym sessions in them, and while sweat does build up after intense workouts, it dries way faster than other leggings I’ve tried thanks to its high nylon content in the fabric. I also love how the fabric feels light, breathable, and cool against the skin, so it doesn’t cause overheating like some of my other leggings. That mentioned, I only own these in darker colors, so I can’t speak to how well they hide sweat stains on lighter shades.

I’ve tried a ton of pieces from Rhone, like its workout dress and bra tops, but my favorites are these pocket leggings, which have tons of storage for my belongings, just enough compression, and maximum softness.

Unlike many other pocketed leggings I’ve tried, these offer a sleek look—you can barely even notice the pockets. While discreet, the pockets still hold a ton. I can even fit my iPhone in them, and thanks to the pockets’ compression, it won’t slip out. Unlike most leggings with pockets, these don’t add any bulk to the thighs for a flattering finish.

Sources indicate that I’ve worn these leggings during many different types of workouts, and they always strike the perfect balance of support and comfort. These are soft enough for a stretching or yoga class, but really shine in any exercise that gets your heart rate pumping and the sweat flowing. Plus, the moisture-wicking fabric and its odor-fighting finish keep me feeling fresh, even when things get super sweaty.

I’m also a mega fan of the wide waistband that stays put through any exercise. And get this: If you’re out in the sun, these leggings add a great extra layer of defense to your sunscreen, as they’re equipped with UPF 50 for sun protection.

In a recent development, my one con with these leggings is that they run large, as does all of Rhone’s womenswear. I would size down if you’re looking for a normal fit with light compression.

Beyond Yoga leggings in their signature (super soft) Spacedye fabric have been my go-to for lounging and low-impact yoga for years. But recently, the activewear label dropped Glowzone, its upcoming high-performance line with a snappy fabric designed to support intense, sweaty movement while still offering the comfort we know and love.

The Glowzone fabric is made of smooth nylon and a bit more elastane than the brand’s famed Spacedye fabric, giving it noticeably more compression. It’s snappy and compressive enough that it keeps me feeling supported and locked-in during my workouts without restricting movement or sliding down my waist (something I often have trouble with while wearing other compressive leggings).

Sources indicate that despite the more snappy fabric, it’s every bit as soft and comfortable as I’d expect from a pair of Beyond Yoga leggings. I still reach for mine on more chill days spent walking the boardwalk near the beach or running errands around town—but the material is just a touch too compressive to wear for lazy days spent couch rotting. Where it really shines is for working out: I’ve worn it to the gym for cardio and lifting sessions as well as mat Pilates classes, and I love that I can basically forget about what I’m wearing while I focus on getting my reps in.

Contributor Sidney Lee tested a few items from the Glowzone collection and agrees the fabric is every bit as soft as she hoped. “It’s slightly thinner than Spacedye, which makes Glowzone feel sleeker and more breathable against the skin,” she claims. “Also, the four-way stretch and moisture-wicking technology of the newly introduced fabric offer more freedom of movement, especially during heated classes or summer workouts.”.

Another huge bonus? This pair is basically seamless (the only seams are located on the inside of the legs and at the buttock) so there’s no rubbing or chafing. There’s no front seam (which helps keep the fit looking flattering, if you know what I mean), and it has raw edges at the bottom, which means the legging basically melts into your skin.

Not only that, but they’re made with breathable mesh dots to help keep you cool during tough workouts. Of all the leggings I’ve tested, this pair does the best job of keeping me sweat-free even after the most intense sweat sessions. Even after a particularly grueling Barry’s class, I was dry by the time I walked out the door.

It has been revealed that this legging is nearly seamless—the only seams are on the back buttock area— which helps shape the glutes—and on the inside of each leg. I love that there’s no front seam (way more comfy and flattering!) and that the few seams necessary here are totally flat and don’t cause any rubbing or discomfort.

According to recent reports, lauture adds that this pair of leggings also does a great job at holding you in. “It might take you a few moments of jumping up and down to get them on, but they feel great on your body once you get them up,” she says. These leggings lean on the compressive side, but tighter leggings are great for higher intensity workouts because they hold you in. So, if you’re into HIIT, running, or strength training, this is another solid pair. Since they’re slightly tighter, I find that they shape and sculpt your body in all the right places.

There are no pockets at the legs or in the waistband of these leggings, so if you don’t need storage, these are a great option.

Industry observers note that unlike the lulu pair on this list, these have less compression, which I prefer for low-impact workouts. They don’t squeeze too much or make my skin bunch up, so I can move freely and comfortably in any move.

And, the pockets in these leggings come in handy post-workout when you’re off running errands and need an easy place to store your key, credit card, or AirPods. But, they don’t add much width to the hips and have a flattering fit, which isn’t always the case with leggings with pockets. During testing, I found that these literally feel like a second skin—they are so soft and lightweight. Because they’re low compression, they’re also super comfortable for lounging.

According to recent reports, like the Rhone leggings, these are treated with UPF 40, so I like to wear them out for long walks on sunny days because they provide a solid extra layer of sun protection. And, if it really starts to get warm out, they have a quick-drying fabric that’s made with a high nylon content. However, stylist Rose Lauture says that although sweat stains fade quickly, she does notice they show easily in the leggings' lighter colors.

Industry observers note that of all the leggings I've tested, Spanx has the best smoothing fabric. They’re not super compressive (which is why I love them for low-impact exercises), but the fabric is insanely soft, sweat-wicking, and buttery smooth.

Recent findings suggest that “Just like the brand's famed shapewear, these are super flattering, with light stomach compression that snatches your waist, and a back waistband design that slightly dips down to enhance the shape of your booty,” claims Wohlner. Their lack of a front seam also makes them much more flattering and so easy to style with anything from a sports bra to a cropped sweater.

I’ve tried a high-intensity workout in these leggings and didn’t feel super supported, so if you’re looking for a pair that can hold you in during deep squats and burpees, these are not my strongest recommendation.

Alo's High-Waist Airbrush Leggings are super versatile because they’re nice and compressive for the gym, and their sleek look plays well with all my casual fits for a chic brunch look.

I’ve struggled to find a pair of high-waisted compression leggings that actually stay up, but these never roll down when I’m moving or sitting, which I appreciate. Plus, they’re on the thinner side, so they don’t feel constrictive like a sausage casing. They stay where I want them for my entire workout and never make me feel claustrophobic.Another pro? The soft material, which has a super smooth, matte look that makes them a bit dressier. Even with sneakers and a zip-up, I find that these make my gym fits look super chic. I deem these leggings worth the buy because of how versatile they are, but shelling out $118 is no easy spend for leggings. So, I like to keep my eye out for a sale where I can get these leggings at a discount.My only gripe is that they run small. I’d recommend sizing up for a more comfortable fit—otherwise, they might feel too tight and could end up rolling down.

When we first wrote this story in March 2025, we rounded up our all-time favorite leggings for workouts after testing each pair at the gym, on long runs, around the house, and on long days out and about to see which ones earned top marks across comfort, support, compression, style, breathability, and moisture-wicking abilities. Over the past few months, I’ve continued to put them through their paces (and tried even more options) to make sure this guide includes all the best workout leggings.

All the winners on this list have been personally vetted and tested by me. I also chatted with style contributor Lily Wohlner as well as stylist and WH contributor Rose Lauture about their favorite pairs, since they are constantly styling and testing leggings, too.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lucid (LCID) claims service wait times dropped 20% globally in the third quarter after it grew its technician and service-support staff by more than 40% in a single quarter.

Recent findings suggest that the automaker is also adding Studio and Service Centers in Southern California, Los Angeles, Dallas, and the Chicago suburbs, plus 20 more Gravity Mobile Service vans. It’s a clear sign that service had become a problem for Lucid owners.

Lucid announced the numbers today, a day after its Q3 2026 earnings. Both comparisons are against the second quarter, not a year ago.

The hiring isn’t done either. After a 40%-plus increase in technicians, advisors, and concierges in Q3, Lucid wants that figure at 50% by the end of 2026 and 60% by Q1 2027. Mobile Service capacity in North America grew 15%, with a 40% target for year-end.

That’s a substantial hiring push for a organization that laid off 18% of its workforce in June, its second cut in four months after a 12% reduction in February. Roughly 1,500 people left across those two rounds.

In a recent development, and owners noticed. On the LucidOwners forum, one Air Touring owner posted in early October that Lucid told them in writing to expect “a service time of about 7 weeks” at its Beverly Hills Service Center. Other threads blamed service-department layoffs for slow repairs and recall work.

Billy Hayes, Lucid’s Chief Customer Officer, mentioned the tech giant is “adding service personnel, and increasing Mobile Service capacity to reduce wait times and provide more convenient, responsive support.”.

Here’s what’s opening, according to Lucid:.

Lucid is also letting a growing number of its Certified Collision shops handle recall campaign work, which should take some pressure off its own Service Centers.

Sources indicate that outside the US, the expansion leans on partners. Munsterhuis Autobedrijven is Lucid’s first retail partner in the Netherlands (Hengelo), Cloppenburg Automobil SE opens a Duisburg retail and service site in January 2027, Autohaus Possögel starts authorized service in Naumburg, Germany, in December, and Emil Frey France will support Lucid’s launch in France. In Saudi Arabia, Lucid opened its first organization-owned Body & Paint Repair Center in Riyadh, with more service sites in Riyadh and Dammam coming in the first half of 2027.

Lucid doesn’t say what the average wait time actually is.

Recent findings suggest that A 20% drop from seven weeks is still more than five weeks. A 20% drop from one week is a non-issue. Without a baseline, owners can’t tell which one they’re getting.

It’s also hard to separate better service from fewer cars coming in. Lucid delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3, down 7% year-over-year, while it worked through inventory. Its fleet keeps growing, but slowly.

For context, Rivian delivered 19,248 vehicles in Q3, five times Lucid’s volume, and it’s been leaning hard on mobile service too. Lucid is a much smaller operation trying to cover the US, Europe, and the Middle East with a thin network.

This is the right move, and it’s overdue.

Recent findings suggest that lucid has been one of the few EV startups with genuinely class-leading hardware. The Air’s efficiency is still unmatched and the Gravity is a great vehicle on paper, even if we found its software wasn’t ready. But when you’re asking someone to spend $80,000 or more on a car from a brand with an uncertain future, the ownership experience is half the sale. A seven-week wait for a repair kills that sale, and the referrals that come after it.

So growing service staff by 40% in a quarter is a big deal. It also tells you how thin those teams had gotten after two rounds of layoffs. Lucid cut too deep in the wrong place, and it’s now hiring to fix it.

In a recent development, the problem is the timing and the money. Lucid burned $1.04 billion in free cash flow in Q3 and only stays funded into late 2027 because the PIF just added another $1.75 billion. Meanwhile, the Midsize “Cosmos” that’s supposed to bring real volume doesn’t start production until the second half of 2027. Service is exactly where Lucid should spend between now and then, because the buyers it has today are the ones who’ll decide whether anybody trusts the brand with a cheaper EV.
